concept.name: Over-the-counter market
concept.definition: A decentralized market in which counterparties negotiate transactions directly or through dealer networks rather than on a centralized exchange, allowing contract terms to be customized. Most foreign exchange, government and corporate bond, and swap trading occurs over the counter.
concept.intuition: Instead of meeting in one hall, buyers and sellers call dealers or message each other directly and agree their own deal terms.
concept.mechanics: Dealers stream or respond with bid and offer quotes by screen or voice; trades are privately negotiated, then subject to applicable post-trade reporting (e.g., to swap data repositories or FINRA TRACE) and, where mandated, central clearing.
concept.failure_modes: Opacity and counterparty credit risk: without a central counterparty each side bears the other's default risk, and limited pre-trade transparency can obscure true prices and let risk concentrate invisibly, as in the 2008 credit default swap market.
concept.misconceptions: OTC does not mean unregulated or exotic — the largest regulated markets (FX, U.S. Treasuries, swaps) trade over the counter, and many OTC derivatives are now subject to mandatory central clearing and reporting.
concept.example: Two banks bilaterally negotiate a five-year interest rate swap; a corporate bond changes hands between dealers over the counter rather than on an exchange.
